articles.summary: Diverging Paths is the first part of the Phantom Blade Zero prologue. This part of the walkthrough is where you’ll learn a bit about our protagonist,
articles.body:
Diverging Paths is the first part of the Phantom Blade Zero prologue. This part of the walkthrough is where you’ll learn a bit about our protagonist, Soul, while getting your first taste of basic movement and combat.

Jump to a specific section of the page using the header links below:

You need to choose a difficulty as soon as you start a new game. There are four options available, and you can change the difficulty at any time during your playthrough.

Wayfarer is the option to pick if you want to focus on the story and fight at your own pace. This is the easiest option, described as “a gentler path through the Wulin.”

Pathbreaker is the traditional medium/normal difficulty setting, providing a challenge for those who are used to action combat. It’s described as “a true test of skill.”

Hellwalker is the hard difficulty setting, for those who want to be thoroughly tested in combat. It’s described as “the ultimate trial.”

66 Days is the hardest difficulty that can only be unlocked after beating the game on any other difficulty. It’s the same as Hellwalker, but you can only die 66 times.

I’m writing this walkthrough while playing on Hellwalker to provide the most useful and accurate tips possible for players who may need them. Some notes or details about enemy strength may not apply to those playing on lower difficulties.

The game opens on a duel between two men: Soul and Zuo Shang . They both drop to their knees after trading blows, then we jump 16 years into the past.

Walk forward along the linear path while following the movement tutorials. You can also do a few other actions, even though they’re unnecessary at this point. Here’s a quick list of a few early controls for console and PC:

Eventually, you come to a high ledge. Press X on controller or Space on keyboard to climb up. The path splits, but there’s nothing of note to the left. Keep climbing up the ledges ahead to reach a wall run section.

The scratches you see on ledges and walls indicate areas where you can use traversal techniques to proceed.

Cross the bridge and crouch under the low branch ahead when prompted. When the path splits, you can go in either direction - they lead to the same place.

To the right, you can practice chaining wall runs together, and to the left, you’ll drop down on the other side of those walls. Regardless of which way you go, follow the linear path through the bamboo to trigger a scene.

Zuo Shang is waiting for you at your destination, but Soul wonders why their Shifu still hasn’t returned. It’s time to learn combat basics in the meantime.

Press the Right Stick on controller or the middle mouse button to lock on , then land four light attacks to perform a standard combo.

Next, learn about Sha-Chi , the yellow meter under your health bar. Sha-Chi combos use heavy attacks and consume the yellow meter.

Land any two of the four Sha-Chi combos listed in the tutorial pop-up to pass this part of combat training.

Continuously guarding also consumes Sha-Chi, so you remember not to play too defensively during combat. Hold guard until Zuo Shang’s combo ends to move to the next tutorial pop-up.

You can also deplete an enemy’s Sha-Chi meter and break their guard by continuously attacking them. Hit Zuo Shang with light attacks until his guard is broken. Sha-Chi combos break enemy guards faster than normal ones.

Now, it’s time for defensive options. You can press dodge without a direction to backstep, or choose a direction to dodge that way. Dodge three of Zuo Shang’s attacks to proceed.

Parries will likely be the defensive option you use most often. Block Zuo Shang’s attacks just before they land to parry.

Parry two blue-flash attacks, and dodge two red-flash attacks before they hit to progress. Remember that blue means parry and red means dodge.

You can now unleash a Power Surge by pressing L2 or Q. Power Surges consume a Sha-Chi Essence , shown in the bottom-right corner of the screen. Power Surges are lengthy combos that wear down the enemy’s Sha-Chi meter.

The tutorial quickly turns into a sparring match against Zuo Shang. Your health seems to replenish automatically if it gets too low during this fight, but we’ll treat it like a real boss for some good practice!

He uses all the moves you just had to dodge and parry during the tutorial, and we’ve listed them all in the table below:

First, note that Zuo Shang doesn’t attack unless you’re close to him. You can back away from him if you ever need a second to collect your thoughts or slow down the battle

Use this fight to get used to parry and dodge timing, especially for blue or red flash attacks. Parry blue flashes or dodge red flashes to counterattack automatically, significantly lowering Zuo Shang’s Sha-Chi meter.

Usually, you should mix offense and defense to guard break your opponent, but try not to end this fight until you’re more comfortable with your defensive options – it’s the perfect time to practice . Your health regenerates automatically here, but you can also press Down on the D-Pad or R on keyboard to heal manually.

A cutscene plays immediately after you win. Soul drops to his knees and screams as red energy flows out of him, then we transition back to the rainy day duel from the beginning of the game. It’s time for a more intense fight.

Boss Battle: Zuo Shang, The Order’s Shadow Sovereign

Zuo Shang, The Order’s Shadow Sovereign Boss Phase 1

Use the knowledge and skills you just acquired from the sparring match flashback to defeat Zuo Shang again. You still heal automatically in this one, but his move list is different. We’ve listed his special attacks in the table below:

You aren’t in danger of dying during this fight either, but it’s a good preview of what’s to come for future boss fights. You need to learn to react quickly to attacks, or create space to evade.

Zuo Shang creates several light-based weapons that he throws at you to perform combos. This is another great opportunity to practice your defensive timing because he throws several attacks at you in quick succession.

Offensively, you should mix light and heavy attacks to create Sha-Chi combos that can break Zuo Shang’s guard. After a few combos and defensive successes, you can use Power Surge to deal solid damage and gain an advantage.

Zuo Shang, The Order’s Shadow Sovereign Boss Phase 2

Zuo Shang jumps back onto the roof when he drops below 50% HP. You need to perform a single quick-time event (QTE) by pressing Triangle or F when he launches a piece of the roof toward you.

He only has one big new move in this phase that you should watch out for – another blue-flash attack.

Zuo Shang fires several light blades at you before leaping into the air for a blue-flash attack with a giant sword. Parry as he falls toward you to counterattack.

At this point, you can continue using this fight as parry and dodge practice, or you can go on the full offensive, using Sha-Chi combos and Power Surges to finish off the boss.

Keep in mind that a Power Surge often interrupts Zuo Shang, even if you use it during his combo. Use it to get out of tough situations where you feel overwhelmed.

After the battle, you get to watch the cutscene from the beginning of the game again. This time, it continues, as you see a mysterious being named the Flesh Sculptor offer you a new heart.

They offer the Hollow Heart or the Tainted Heart. The former strips away all emotion and desire, leaving only reason. The latter keeps your heart beating with Venom, but will kill you in 66 days .

Soul chooses the Tainted Heart as this chapter ends. Next up is Reckless Pursuit .

articles.title: Stress Less Walkthrough - Hello Kitty Island Adventure Guide - IGN
articles.summary: ”Stress Less” is a Visitor Quest that unlocks once Anai has become a Permanent Resident in Hello Kitty Island Adventure. Once this quest is
articles.body:
”Stress Less” is a Visitor Quest that unlocks once Anai has become a Permanent Resident in Hello Kitty Island Adventure . Once this quest is complete, you’ll be able to invite Anai out as a Companion when exploring Friendship Island.

To begin the quest, talk to Retsuko in the Hot Springs. She’s noticed something strange about Anai’s behavior since coming to the island. Aside from being a tall bean sprout, you haven’t noticed anything too unusual. Retsuko invites you to investigate with her, but first, you’ll need to learn what you can from Haida .

Follow Retsuko to meet Haida out near Visitor Cabin 4. This cabin on the far west side of Mount Hothead along the beach. Anai and Kabae are nearby, talking to one another. Sneak over to Haida to see what he’s observed. After watching Anai’s interactions with Kabae, Haida actually seems to sense something is off too!

The two coworkers seem worried that Anai might blow a gasket and urge you to follow after Anai with them to make sure he remains chill. Follow the gang to the Hot Springs to observe Anai’s conversation with Ookami . They have plans for chilling out on the beach, but are still missing some drinks for the occasion.

Retsuko and Haida are certain that something is up with Anai, who then appears! He asks if the two are meddling again, to which Retsuko immediately denies. Anai then asks if you might have supplies on hand since you’ve been on the island longer!

Give Anai 2x Coconuts ( Seaside Resort ) and 3x Banana Sodas to help him out.

Banana Soda Recipe: 1x Fizzy Crystal (Crafted from Fizzy Ore, Obtained from Gemstone Mines) and 1x Banana ( Pompompurin’s Daily Gift)

Anai goes back to hang out with Ookami, and Retsuko ponders over this sudden change. Maybe she’ll just have to get used to this other side of Anai… Before she can finish the thought, though, Haida exclaims that Anai is on the move again!

Follow the two to Gemstone Beach, where Anai has met up with Yoga Instructor . Watching Anai be so stress-free is somehow becoming all that more stressful for Haida and Retsuko. But Anai isn’t falling for it anymore. He asks for your group to join him instead of just following him around the island.

Anai explains that he’s more relaxed outside of work because he’s on vacation. Retsuko can’t relate. Anai says that it’s easier to not worry or stress because he’s not answering his emails, unlike a certain someone.

Almost on cue, Retsuko’s phone starts going off with end notifications. She resists for two whole notifications before she has to check her phone. Chief Komiya wants to gather everyone for an announcement. Anai advises that Retsuko would feel much better if she put her phone on Do Not Disturb.

He manages to convince everyone to do some yoga to relax, and after a quick session, Anai excuses himself to follow up on a spa treatment he had scheduled with the Seaponies. With the quest complete, you can now invite Anai out as a chill companion to keep you company while adventuring around Friendship Island.

Additionally, “Dread Honcho” will become available. In this quest, it’s finally happening. Chief Komiya has figured out a way to invite the one person Retsuko doesn’t want to see on her vacation.

articles.title: Reckless Pursuit Walkthrough - Phantom Blade Zero Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Reckless Pursuit is the second part of the Phantom Blade Zero prologue. This walkthrough picks up after you learn about Soul’s venom-filled
articles.body:
Reckless Pursuit is the second part of the Phantom Blade Zero prologue. This walkthrough picks up after you learn about Soul’s venom-filled heart.

Jump to a specific section of the page using the header links below:

This chapter begins as Soul journeys to a town named Pangzhen while speaking to a traveler named Old Man Gen . He tells Soul that there’s a plague there, causing townsfolk to lose their minds.

People have also seen lifelike wooden puppets near the town, pulled by strings. Soul believes it’s a phenomenon called Soul Displacement caused by the Thread-Binding Sect .

Reckless Pursuit is a fitting title because you’re thrust into a chase scene as two enemies interrupt your conversation with Old Man Gen.

This is a bit of an on-rails action segment – you don’t need to steer the cart right now. Hold block to block all incoming gunshots until you see a blue flash from one of the gunmen. Parry as soon as you see the flash to counterattack.

Then, block more incoming bullets until you see a red flash. Dodge the red flash to counter and trigger a quick scene that changes the camera angle.

The enemies are now on either side of you, in melee range. You can block or parry all of their normal strikes, then pay attention to the colors of their combo finishers. Parry the blue flashes and dodge the red flashes.

Attack with your own standard or Sha-Chi combo once you’ve parried or dodged a combo finisher. Press Circle on controller or E on keyboard to execute an enemy when the prompt shows up on their body.

A third assailant appears after you beat the first two. This time, it’s a one-on-one fight in the carriage bed.

Approach it the same way as you did the other two – block or parry standard slashes, and watch for blue or red flashes. Another scene plays after you defeat that one. It’s time for a high-speed boss fight.

Boss Battle: The Hunt, Hunter of the Order

The Hunt is a sickle-wielding spectral entity who is chasing Soul because he attacked Zuo Shang, the Shadow Sovereign. This fight takes place on the carriage bed, so there isn’t much room to move. Here are all the special attacks you need to watch out for:

There isn’t much room for movement since you’re on a carriage here. Dodging doesn’t always work out as intended because of the limited space, so rely more on blocking and parrying here, especially when The Hunt’s attacks speed up.

Aim for standard or Sha-Chi combos whenever The Hunt is standing inside the carriage bed with you. Focus more on defense when the boss is standing on the horses and attacking from a distance.

You only have to get The Hunt down to about 50% HP to trigger a cutscene that brings the fight to an end. This is another named enemy who doesn’t feel like a true boss fight, but we’ll get to one soon.

Soul slashes The Hunt to end the encounter, then tries to leap across a huge chasm as the road ends. He falls down into a whole different area while remembering the Flesh Sculptor’s words from the day before.

The Flesh Sculptor said that there’s a Heart in Pangzhen that can remake flesh and raise the dead, and he’ll use that heart to allow Soul to live beyond 66 days.

That quick flashback brings an end to Reckless Pursuit . Next up, we enter the Weeping Creek Valley for Against the Flow .

articles.title: Weeping Creek Sha-Chi Amber Fragment Locations - Phantom Blade Zero Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Throughout the Weeping Creek Valley in Phantom Blade Zero, you'll find four different Sha-Chi Amber Fragments. Collecting all four will give you one full
articles.body:
Throughout the Weeping Creek Valley in Phantom Blade Zero, you'll find four different Sha-Chi Amber Fragments. Collecting all four will give you one full Amber Fragment which can be used to upgrade one of your abilities at any of the nearby Bells around.

Weeping Creek Valley Sha-Chi Amber Fragments

You may not be able to hit every Sha-Chi Amber immediately, as some require collecting a Phantom Edge before being able to progress or open a new area. Below you'll find the locations of all four Amber Fragments.

Weeping Creek Valley Sha-Chi Amber Fragment 1

On the main path south of the Broken Puppet Valley Bell. You'll discover a headless enemy with a shield. Defeat the group of enemies here, including the headless knight and you'll find the Sha-Chi Amber Fragment in the purple glowing chest.

Weeping Creek Valley Sha-Chi Amber Fragment 2

You'll obtain this Amber Fragment after defeating a group of enemies northeast of the Rustblade Pavillion Bell. Luckily, this one is on the main story path, so you won't miss it.

Weeping Creek Valley Sha-Chi Amber Fragment 3

Just north of the Outpost Bell you'll see a wall that can be broken using the Dread Axe Phantom Edge. Destroy the wall and clear out the enemies in the newly open section. Upon killing the last enemy you'll automatically get the next Sha-Chi Amber Fragment

Weeping Creek Valley Sha-Chi Amber Fragments 4

From the Long Pillar Overlook Bell, go across the wooden bridge. From here follow the path on the right hand side. This will include wall running over a small gap. Keep going straight until you see a small metal door in the rockface.Use the Rusted Long Key on door on the sound of the mountain. INside there are a few enemies; dispatch all of them to get the final Sha-Chi Amber Fragment found in this section

Enjoy your new Amber Fragment now that you've got all four fragments found in the Weeping Creek Valley. Be sure to grab the Blackstone Fragments while you're here before moving on to the Crimson Forest.

articles.title: GTA 6's Map Will Open Up Relatively Early and Let You Explore Freely, Developers Are Still Discovering New Parts of the World
articles.summary: GTA 6's world won't be blocked off by story progression, Rockstar confirms.
articles.body:
GTA 6's world won't be blocked off by story progression, Rockstar confirms.

In a new preview from Edge magazine (as relayed by the podcast GTA VI O'Clock ), Rockstar Games confirmed a ton of new details about GTA 6. One of the big bits revealed was that GTA 6's map will open up relatively early. In some GTA games, like GTA 4, the game forces you to progress through its story before you can access the entire map. GTA 4's Liberty City uses police blockades on bridges to make sure the world only expands as Niko continues his journey. That changed in GTA 5, as you could go wherever your heart desired once the game's tutorials were finished.

It seems like GTA 6 will be similar, as Edge's story confirms that the state of Leonida will open up relatively early on. Of course, there will likely be some initial story bits to introduce the characters and mechanics before you can go wherever you want. So, if you wish to head north and see the top of the map at the start of the game, you can do so. Of course, the story itself will take you to a lot of places around the map as you experience it, but you won't be chained to Vice City for the first 10 hours if you don't want to be.

Even More GTA 6 Screenshots from Rockstar Games

Red Dead Redemption 2 also largely lets the player freely explore the map, but there was one area that they couldn't visit until the end of the game: the entire map from the first Red Dead Redemption. While there wasn't as much to see and do there, it was a fun surprise that almost doubled the scope of the game's map. If players tried to go there before the story was ready, they would be shot and killed by snipers.

Similarly, the first Red Dead Redemption game prevented the player from visiting Mexico until John Marston's journey took him there. It seems like GTA 6 will give players a lot of freedom off the bat... and it may take a while before you see anything. Rockstar North co-studio head Aaron Garbut also confirmed that he's still discovering new locations in Leonida.

Part of that comes from how dense the game is, with Garbut noting that there are "an order of magnitude more interiors" compared to other Rockstar titles, and all of them have been handcrafted with an exceptional level of detail.

GTA 6 will release on November 19 for Xbox Series X|S and PS5.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

articles.title: A Famous GTA 4 Meme Is Now a Mechanic in GTA 6
articles.summary: GTA 6 has named one of its biggest mechanics after a beloved GTA 4 meme.
articles.body:
GTA 6 has named one of its biggest mechanics after a beloved GTA 4 meme.

In 2008, a Justin.tv channel (now known as Twitch) by the name of FourPlayerPodcast made GTA history. One of the hosts of the channel, Brad Simons, rode a moped around GTA 4's Liberty City. He eventually found another moped rider and began comically declaring them "scooter brothers." The video has over 7.5 million views on YouTube , and now it's part of GTA 6.

In a new preview from Edge magazine , it was confirmed that players will be able to summon their vehicle using an app called Scooter Brothers. An NPC will deliver your car and then get on a scooter (presumably driven by another "brother") and drive off. Whether or not these so-called scooter brothers will have their own silly lines to honor their origins remains to be seen.

GTA 6 Reveal: 15 New Screenshots, Including 1 Exclusive on IGN

In GTA 5, when switching to Trevor, players would have a chance of seeing the wily character recreating the meme with a frightened NPC. It was a pretty great nod, and now, Rockstar is keeping the tradition alive, though this time with more purpose.

GTA Online has had a mechanic to let you call your car since launch, and Red Dead Redemption also allows you to summon your horse if it's within a reasonable distance. However, this is the first time players will be able to do something like this without cheats in GTA's single-player. It's arguably more necessary than ever, too, as the player's arsenal of weapons and some other important gear is stored in the trunk of their vehicle. It also means your cars likely won't be as disposable as they were in previous games.

All of this news comes just three weeks ahead of GTA 6's launch and two weeks before pre-loading begins. Rockstar's marketing efforts are ramping up across the globe . Rumors also indicate a PC version of the game is just around the corner, with a reported release window of early 2027 . Either way, it's an exciting time to be a GTA fan.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

articles.title: Against the Flow Walkthrough - Phantom Blade Zero Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Against the Flow is the first major quest in Phantom Blade Zero. This chapter picks up as Soul falls into a large valley after his high-speed fight against The
articles.body:
Against the Flow is the first major quest in Phantom Blade Zero . This chapter picks up as Soul falls into a large valley after his high-speed fight against The Hunt. This walkthrough will guide you through the first half of Weeping Creek Valley.

Jump to a specific section of the page using the header links below:

This chapter begins as Soul wakes up after falling far down into Weeping Creek Valley. Hold Triangle or F to get up, then heal and open the map using the touchpad on controller or M/Tab on keyboard.

Yellow quest markers indicate main objectives that’ll lead you toward Zuo Shang. Purple quest markers indicate side quests that can change the outcome of Soul’s fate.

White scroll quest markers indicate Wulin Tales , which can provide useful info for boss fights or exploration.

You’ll also notice that there’s a red square on the map, marking an item that you can’t yet obtain. First, you need to find The Hunter’s Chain Sickle weapon.

For now, follow the path forward, under the hanging horse, until you hear someone crying. The Whence the Weeping side quest is then added to your quest list.

You can interact with the petrified body and sword on either side of the stream for a bit of extra info. There’s also a currency called Remnant Dust near the sword. Climb the scratched rock ledge to your left to proceed to the next area.

Just ahead, you’ll encounter your first Maskwalker brute . This common enemy type appears throughout this area. They have low health and can be dispatched quickly with standard combos. But be ready to parry their blue-flash attacks when necessary.

Maskwalker brutes can be overwhelmed if you stay on the offensive. Don’t be afraid to unleash combos before they get a chance to attack you.

Drop down to your right to collect some Remnant Dust, then help the man ahead by defeating a pair of Maskwalkers.

The dying escapee tells you he came from upstream and asks that you save the village there. That’s our next destination.

Collect the Remnant Dust in the water, then climb the large scratched stone near the man’s body.

Walk forward until Soul mentions being pulled by something. Red strings are pulling you toward a bell on the path. A woman named Inani tells you that the bells ring only for you, and they’ll heal your wounds.

Bells function as rest spots, restoring HP and medicine. Touch a bell for the first time to reveal new sections of the surrounding area on the map. You can also train abilities and save at bells.

You should always follow red strings if you ever see them attached to Soul’s body – especially if you’re in a new area. It means that you’re near a bell. This bell is called The Beginning .

Select the Train Abilities option at the bell to enter a quick tutorial. Use Blackstones , Sha-Chi Ambers , and Large Memory Flowers to increase your attributes and unlock new abilities.

You also use Remnant Dust to activate unlocked abilities. The first unlock is free in this tutorial, and you can also refund all unlocked abilities to regain all Remnant Dust.

You’re forced to refund Fluid Form Lv. 1, but you should acquire it again before exiting the training menu since it’s still free.

Walk past the waterfall ahead and into another clearing where two Maskwalkers are waiting. As the game suggests, you should prioritize ranged enemies. Melee attackers are tougher to handle when long-range enemies hit you from different angles.

The next group of Maskwalkers is a group of four around a fire. None are ranged, but the one with a flaming weapon is the most dangerous. Remember to lock on to your target and execute them when prompted.

You’re invulnerable during execution animations, so take advantage of them. And oftentimes, one or two successful parries can trigger the execution prompt on these basic Maskwalkers.

You can read the writing on the wall near the fire, then walk over to the waterfall in front of you to fight a Yellow-Robed Brute . This Maskwalker variant is a bit tougher, so prepare to block or parry his club.

Pick up the Remnant Dust under the falls, then climb the scratched rock on the nearby ledge. It leads to a path that goes up a large branch and some scaffolding. A short scene plays when you cross the branch, as a creature’s roar is heard in the distance.

Three Maskwalkers are waiting for you at the top of the stairs. Take out the stone-throwing enemy first, then the other two.

Pick up the note titled Investigating the Villagers’ Belongings: Abandoned Land Deed . It’s on the ground, just past a ladder.

Climb the ladder to get a quick stealth tutorial. Press the Left Stick on controller or C on keyboard to crouch, then press execute when behind an unaware enemy to assassinate them.

The screen borders darken when you sneak up behind an unsuspecting enemy – that’s how you know you’re doing it right.

You can also perform assassinations after wall runs. Wall run across the gap ahead, then press the execute prompt when you reach the next Maskwalker.

Watch out for the next enemy up the steps – they throw fire pots that ignite the ground. Attack quickly or wait until the fire clears to get your chance.

Keep moving along the wooden walkway until you see a ladder to your right. Red strings will attach themselves to Soul from below, so look down to find The Lady’s Rift bell .

Now that you’ve unlocked a second bell, you can use the Traverse option in the bell menu to fast-travel between bells.

You can interact with the golden rift next to the bell to enter an optional boss fight. This Aberrant Three-Faced Puppet boss fight is a tough one early on, so you can always return later with more weapons and abilities.

The Triple Threat side quest is added to your quest log after exiting the rift. Climb back up the ladder near the Lady’s Rift bell and run along the wall ahead to continue.

Pick up the purple-colored item on the ground near the chained fence to obtain the Traversal Talisman – a consumable item used to travel to a bell from anywhere on the map.

Swing across the chain ahead to cross the gap, then defeat the dual-wielding Maskwalker to get the Hunter’s Insight accessory. It increases damage dealt and Sha-Chi depletion against attacking enemies by 7%.

Continue along the wooden walkway to get a tutorial for Mind’s Eye , which is a feature that shows your tracked quest objective marker in the world. Hold down the top part of the touchpad on controller, or press V on keyboard to trigger Mind’s Eye.

Wall run across the next gap, then sprint to the chain hanging from the tree above to swing over to the other side of the gap in front of you.

There are two Maskwalkers tossing fire pots and rocks from the other side, so you need to be quick to avoid getting hit before swinging on the chain. Attack the Maskwalkers immediately to prevent them from pelting you with a barrage of throwables.

Slide down the rope at the end of the cliffside to reach the area below, then walk toward the woman sitting at the campsite.

The woman’s name is Yu’er , daughter of the village brewer, and she’s just escaped from Pangzhen. She’s out here looking for a rare flower to save her father from a mysterious illness that has befallen everyone in the village.

Yu’er also tells you that the road to Pangzhen is through the woods in the valley, above a large waterfall.

You can ask Yu’er about the main road, the weeping woman, and how to save her father. She’s looking for a Flesh Lily for her father, and the Flesh Lily side quest appears in your quest log after speaking to her about it.

Climb the scratched ledge near Yu’er’s campsite and continue along this linear path to find twin blades named Sanguine Twin at the base of a ladder.

You can equip two main weapons at once, so equip Sanguine Twin, and press Left on the D-Pad or 1 on keyboard to switch weapons.

Switching weapons fully restores Sha-Chi, which means you can swap weapons after Sha-Chi combos to lengthen your combo without waiting to recharge the meter. Take advantage of this feature to become relentless on offense when aiming for guard breaks.

There’s a short cooldown after switching weapons, though, so give yourself some time before swapping weapons consecutively.

Climb the ladder to find the First Meeting with Yu’er bell . You can also destroy the boxes near the top of the ladder to obtain Forged Metal – a weapon upgrade material that upgrades one-handed weapons to Lv. 10.

You should also be able to unlock new abilities at this bell. Healing Art is a great choice here if you’re playing on Hellwalker difficulty or above, because it increases your medicine uses by one, giving you an extra heal. Whereas Steady Composure allows you to interrupt enemy attacks after dodging or parrying.

Head toward the waterfall in the distance to find a group of Maskwalkers fighting each other. Before you engage, you should drop down near the first lamp along the road to find a lower path that leads to Remnant Dust and a Traversal Talisman.

Climb back up onto the main road to finish off the stronger enemies who are still alive. They should drop the Battle Wraps accessory, which increases damage dealt to enemies by 5%.

Red strings are blocking the path next to the waterfall, but you can find the Red Thread Barrier bell to the left of that obstacle.

Swing across the gap ahead using the chain in front of the bell, then drop down on the left side of the path to find more Remnant Dust.

Return to the road above and follow the floating red thread overhead to find the source of the red thread barrier blocking your path.

Follow the wooden walkway to find more Maskwalkers waiting for a fight. There’s Solvent on the ground behind the furthest Maskwalker. It’s a universal upgrade material used to upgrade weapons to Lv. 10.

Drop down to the lower level of the valley while still following the red thread. There’s also an Exotic Copper Ingot near the waterfall dead-end in the opposite direction of the main path. It’s another upgrade material that raises Martial-type Phantom Edges to Lv. 10.

Watch out for the two arsonists and three brutes waiting for you along the main path as you return from the waterfall dead-end. Target the arsonists first to avoid fiery complications. One is on a high ledge you can climb, and the other is down in the water. Both can be assassinated if you sneak before engaging the group.

Look for the Broken Puppet Valley bell near the stream after the fight. Then, pick up the glowing green book collectible titled The “Four Axes” Case Files: The Four Axes Rebellion: Calamity on the ground under a tree. Picking up this collectible adds the Four Fierce Axes tale to your quest log.

There’s also another glowing green collectible, titled The Four Axes Rebellion: Chaos , inside the nearby house.

Now, you can walk forward into a small campfire area surrounded by red threads. This is your first battle against a shielded enemy. Aim for blue-flash attack parries to land counterattacks from behind.

Shielded enemies often block frontal attacks, so you need a mix of movement and counters to defeat them. Open the chest in the campground after the duel to obtain your first Sha-Chi Amber Fragment . Collect four of these to increase your maximum Sha-Chi by 10%.

The red threads blocking the path near the Red Thread Barrier bell vanish after you win. Return there and walk toward the opening to trigger a scene. Two Maskwalkers ambush you, but the Hunt drags them away, saying that he’s waiting for you.

Proceed under the red threads and pick up the Wulin Tales: Captain Chen Zhu’s Secret Letter collectible on a corpse next to a lantern.

You can speak to the dying Iron Mask at the next lantern along the path for a bit of extra dialogue. Then, walk through the waterfall ahead to enter a fight against an unexpected boss.

Boss Battle: Jagged Steel, the Frenzied Brute

Jagged Steel, the Frenzied Blade , is your opponent here. You can wait a bit to see what he does to the other opponents nearby, but it’ll be your turn to fight soon. Here are all the special attacks you need to look out for:

The dying Iron Mask warned you about a rusty blade that makes you bleed, and he was talking about Frenzied Brute’s sword, Jagged Steel. Every one of his hits causes Bleed buildup, which drains your health. Do your best to avoid taking hits, either by parrying, dodging, or simply creating distance.

Use your new Sanguine Twin blades to extend your Sha-Chi combos by swapping weapons when your Sha-Chi runs low. You can also swap weapons defensively to refill your Sha-Chi meter before a guard break, allowing you to block more attacks. But watch for when the boss’s Sha-Chi meter refills – he’ll instantly start attacking again, ignoring and interrupting your combo.

Be ready to switch from offense to defense instantly whenever the Frenzied Brute recovers from being guard-broken. He also starts using longer combos under 50% HP, so try to be more patient as the battle goes on.

You obtain the Jagged Steel blade after winning the fight. It’s a solid early-game status-effect weapon that inflicts Bleed on enemies as you land hits. You can replace either Sanguine or Sanguine Twin to equip it.

The Rustblade Pavilion bell is at the foot of the steps ahead, but you can also look to the right and crouch under some debris to pick up x2 Twinned Metal. It’s another upgrade material used to raise Dual-Wielded weapons to Lv. 10.

Steady Composure is a good ability to unlock at the bell here, especially if you’ve gotten used to parrying or dodging. But you should also have enough Remnant Dust for Boundless Capacity, which gives you another accessory slot.

Climb the steps in front of the bell and stop when you see a scratched ledge. Look to the left of the ledge to read the writing on the wall and gain x180 Remnant Dust.

To the right, you’ll see a table with a green collectible on it, titled Reflections: Outposts, Rare Places of Rest .

Now, climb the ledges and prepare to be ambushed by three Maskwalkers. Don’t let them surround you, and watch for the dual-wielder’s multi-hit attack. You’re rewarded with a Sha-Chi Amber Fragment after the encounter.

Pick up the x898 Remnant Dust along the path, then open the chest ahead to obtain Ancient Timber. It upgrades Ranged-type Phantom Edges to Lv. 10. You also receive x2 Twinned Metal.

Swing across the gap using the chain near the chest, then follow the path until you reach tall grass. Look left to see x224 Remnant Dust on a wooden overlook.

Crouch-walk into the tall grass, then assassinate the Maskwalker near the campfire. Crouch into the next patch of grass and do the same to the next Maskwalker as well.

You should see another campfire in the distance with more enemies surrounding it. There’s x217 Remnant Dust on the left side of the path, and the Outpost Courtyard bell is waiting for you on the far side of the campfire.

You can chain assassinations together if you execute one unaware enemy near another unaware enemy. Press the prompt that appears on-screen after the first assassination to keep the combo going. Try this with the two Maskwalkers at the campfire.

Continue down the ledges, past the Outpost Courtyard bell. You can see a collectible titled The Four Axes Rebellion: Confusion in the building ahead, and x3 Solvent on the roof, but watch out for the Maskwalkers waiting for you around that building. There’s also x2 Solvent on the path leading up to that roof.

Drop down onto the enemies around this next campfire to assassinate from above, and remember to press the prompt to chain the executions.

Walk into the next area along the main path near the campfire to enter an ambush . Several Maskwalkers appear, but you’re aided by guards who realize you aren’t an enemy.

The battle goes smoothly with their help, but look to the left of the gate before you report to the guards. There’s x437 Remnant Dust near a locked door with a purple item on the other side.

You can’t open the door without a cell key, so speak to the guards at the gate to proceed. They say anyone going to Pangzhen now is a madman, but they let you through.

Enter the outpost and pick up the purple item on the broken cart. It’s a Reforge Talisman – an item that restores a weapon to its initial level. Speak to the woman leaning on the post to learn more about the situation in the outpost.

Speak to the men behind her to find out there’s a Maskwalker bound in chains in the forest near the waterfall. They’re having trouble defeating the threat.

The yellow-robed monk near the bamboo, Huijue , says he needs to find his master, Bi Hai , in the Village of Lu . Soul offers to help, so that may turn into another side quest soon.

You can also trade with the peddler in the building next to the horse, along the main road. He doesn’t have anything you need at this very moment, but keep in mind that he sells weapon upgrade materials.

From the peddler’s shack , look up and to the right. The first building on the hill contains x3 Solvent and x2 Phantom Reforge Talismans, which restore a Phantom Edge to its initial level.

You can also speak to the man in that same building to learn about the Axemaster, which will update the Four Fierce Axes tale in your quest log.

There’s a man – the Brooding Old Archer – on the roof of the next building over as well. Climb up the scratched section in front of him to reach the roof.

Speak to him to add the Purge the Sect tale to your quest log, then pick up the x2 Forged Metal underneath the roof he’s sitting on.

Continue up the stairs along the main path to trigger a scene with a woman named Forge . Inanis sent her here to help you, and her two sisters are elsewhere, waiting to do the same. You can ask Forge about her sisters, Sanguine, and how to obtain weapons.

The youngest sister, Jewel , specializes in jewelry, and the middle sister, Myst , focuses on Phantom Arts.

Exhaust all of Forge’s dialogue options to gain access to her weapon upgrades. You can finally use those upgrade materials you’ve been collecting!

Each weapon type uses different upgrade materials, so focus on upgrading your favorite weapon of each type at this early stage in the game. Don’t split upgrade materials between two weapons of the same type at this point – it’s not worth it.

You should use different upgraded weapon types in combat to get the most out of your materials. Upgrade your two favorites as much as possible here.

Pick up the Sanguine Reach weapon next to Forge to add a two-handed weapon to your arsenal. You likely won’t be able to upgrade it yet, but you can still use it if you like the moveset.

Upgrade Sanguine Twin and one of the one-handed swords, then pick up the x4 Solvent in the bucket next to Forge before returning to the path.

The guards across from Forge give you the Festering Secret tale before you leave the area as well. The Outpost bell is to the right of Forge, and you can now upgrade your weapons or buy the peddler’s items directly in the bell menu.

It’s better to save your Remnant Dust for abilities, as you’ll likely find plenty of upgrade materials through exploration.

You can’t cross the bridge to the left of the bell, so head up the stairs to the right to continue toward the main quest objective.

The path splits at the top of the stairs. Left is progress, and to the right, you’ll find several useful items. Let’s go right first to pick up x2 Darkfire Charcoal, x2 Solvent, x441 Remnant Dust, and the Cell Key for the locked door where you first entered the Outpost.

Run all the way back to that first Outpost gate and use the Cell Key to obtain a Blackstone Fragment. Collect four of these to increase attack and guard break by 10% permanently.

Now, return to the split path at the top of the stairs where you found the Cell Key. Head left this time to trigger a scene that leads straight into a boss fight.

Peng Meng, the Axemaster, breaks free from his chains just as you arrive. He’s a large opponent with plenty of strong strikes, so prepare yourself. These are the special attacks you need to look out for in this fight:

The Axemaster is a slow-moving boss who hits extremely hard. Oftentimes, it’s safer to dodge than attempt a parry, but you’ll want at least a few successful parries to lower his Sha-Chi meter and cause a guard break.

The Axemaster has slow recovery animations after big hits, so stay patient and counterattack when he’s on the ground or regaining his balance. The Jagged Steel sword is great here because it inflicts Bleed and the boss is slow enough to give you generous combo openings.

You earn the Dread Axe after the battle. This is your first Phantom Edge – a secondary weapon that you can equip alongside your main weapons. You also automatically obtain a collectible titled The Axemaster’s Final Request .

Interact with the Crane Bell that appears to see a flashback in which Soul and Zuo Shang fight off an assailant known as the Ethereal Swordsman as children 23 years ago. They also meet a man named Mu Tianmiao, who offers to teach them in the Wulin.

Find Crane Bells to see more of Zuo Shang’s memories to reveal a truth.

Some Phantom Edges, like the Dread Axe, also offer traversal options to unlock new areas in the map. Press R2 on controller or Left CTRL on keyboard to break through chained barriers. Phantom Edges consume a resource called Remnant Sparks, marked by a red swirl icon.

This part of the Festering Secret side quest leads to finding over 600 Remnant Dust and a Sha-Chi Fragment inside the Outpost. You should at least obtain the Sha-Chi Fragment and speak to Yu’er before progressing.

Remember to unlock a new ability and upgrade the Dread Axe as well. The Ascendance Lv. 1 ability is useful because it increases Sha-Chi essence by one and also leads to more healing-related abilities. The choice is yours.

Use the Dread Axe to break through the chain barrier in front of the Axemaster’s Fall Crane Bell to proceed with the main quest.

Walk through the water and up the hill, picking up the x216 Remnant Dust near stacked boxes along the road. Approach the corpse at the top of the hill to trigger a scene with the Hunt. You can actually see him perched on a roof in the distance, staying completely still.

The Hunt slaughtered everyone in this settlement. He taunts Soul, then leaves the area. There’s plenty to interact with here, including The Axemaster’s Holding Cell bell .

Ring the bell, then pick up the collectible near the campfire, titled Captain Wu’s Final Letter . There’s also x2 Forged Metal and a Weapon Reforge Talisman inside the torchlit building nearby.

You should also check the unlit buildings and narrow paths around this settlement to find the Inventory Report collectible, x2 Solvent, and Remnant Dust.

When you're ready, leave through the eastern exit to end this chapter. The Against the Flow chapter ends here. Next up, we have the Steel and Steam chapter.

articles.title: Steel and Steam Walkthrough - Phantom Blade Zero Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Steel and Steam is the second chapter in Phantom Blade Zero. This chapter picks up shortly after defeating the Axemaster and having another run-in with the
articles.body:
Steel and Steam is the second chapter in Phantom Blade Zero . This chapter picks up shortly after defeating the Axemaster and having another run-in with the Hunt. This walkthrough will guide you through the second half of Weeping Creek Valley.

Jump to a specific section of the page using the header links below:

This chapter begins as you leave the Axemaster’s Holding Cell area through its eastern exit. Your new Dread Axe can open up the chain barrier path to your left , and two shielded Maskwalkers are blocking the bridge directly in front of you.

The path on the left leads to a northern dead-end, where you’ll find x3 Forged Metal, the Battle Report collectible, Remnant Dust, and a chest containing Focus Pill medicine. There’s also a Traversal Talisman hidden behind the boxes near the chest.

Soul also notes that he can see a crimson forest steeped in Sha-Chi in the distance – a quick hint at the next location.

Return to the broken chain barrier and look down to your left to see Blood-Stopper Vine guarded by several Maskwalkers. This is one of the three medicinal herbs Yu’er needs for her Apprentice Healer side quest.

Don’t let the Maskwalkers surround you. You can lure them up out of the water to maintain an advantage.

Then, instead of returning to the bridge above, check the path in the water below the bridge. There’s a small chest there containing x2 Broadplate Metal, which upgrades two-handed weapons. The chest also contains Forged Metal and Remnant Dust.

Return to the bridge to fight the two shielded Maskwalkers. Heavy weapons like the Dread Axe can destroy shields . Hold the button/key to charge the axe hit until you see a red flash on Soul, then let go to unleash an extremely powerful heavy combo.

Cross the bridge and pick up the x2 Solvent on the other side before continuing down the path. Destroy the chain gate blocking the road to find a giant tower in the next area.

Quickly turn to your right and walk back the way you came to find Ancient Timber on an elevated wooden platform. There’s also x223 Remnant Dust inside a cage on the right side of the path, further down.

Speak to the Mandate Disciple near the cage, and he’ll warn you to go around the Sha-Chi Tower. Of course, we’re going inside.

Walk across the bridge ahead and approach the bell. The nearby disciple tells you he dropped the base camp gate key inside the Steel Tower while escaping faceless enemies. This begins the Deep in the Valley purple quest.

Interact with the Creek Valley Plains Entrance bell and choose an ability to unlock. This time, Boundless Capacity Lv. 1 is a solid option because you’ll find new accessories soon. Head up the hill to approach the tower when ready.

A scene plays at the top of the hill, showing the Hunt killing more people on his way to the Steel Tower in the distance.

A group of Maskwalkers is ahead, and two archers fire down on you from above. Lure the Maskwalkers on the ground back down the hill you came up, so you’re not caught out in the open as arrows rain down.

You can also parry or block arrows , so listen for the sound they make as they get fired through the air. You can also go straight for the archers and target them first to save some hassle. There’s one to the left on a large pipe, and the other is to the right on an elevated platform.

Pick up the Darkfire Charcoal at the well in the middle of the area after the battle, then continue down the road until you see more elevated wooden platforms.

Climb the ladder on the right to reach the next archer who’s also shooting arrows from above. There’s also x3 Solvent at the foot of the next ladder, where the archer was standing.

Climb the ladder next to the Solvent to reach another archer. This time, he isn’t facing you. Sneak up and assassinate this one to avoid open combat, then turn to your right to pick up the Sha-Chi Tower Ruins collectible inside the house behind you.

Jump down to fight several Maskwalkers below, then take the path to the right to confront another archer. The final archer is sniping from up near a chest, and you receive a Blackstone Fragment and a Broken-String Bow when you defeat him.

Pick up x2 Darkfire Charcoal on the way up to the chest, then open it to obtain the Token of Pursuit accessory. It increases damage dealt to guard-broken enemies by 7%. You can also pick up the Garrison Log collectible to the left of the chest.

Walk up the stairs next to the chest to find the Ruthless Archer Camp bell . You can use it to fast-travel back to the Outpost. But first, pick up the Weapon Reforge Talisman in the room ahead and speak to the dying archer for extra dialogue. There’s also Remnant Dust behind the shack.

Defeating all of those archers is part of the Purge the Sect side quest. You can bring the Broken-String Bow to the Old Archer back at the Outpost to complete the quest.

There should be three spots on the map where you can immediately put your new bow to good use: Near the Old Archer at the Outpost, near the Creek Valley Plains Entrance bell, and near the Ruthless Archer Camp bell.

Now, from the Ruthless Archer Camp bell, cross the bridge leading to the Steel Tower. Be ready to dodge flaming projectiles from an arsonist as you cross.

Three Maskwalkers are waiting for you on the other side of the bridge, to the right of a lone staircase. You’ll find x2 Broadplate Metal behind them. To the left of the staircase is x224 Remnant Dust.

Defeat the Maskwalkers, then climb the stairs to trigger a duel with a Shadow Warden . You fought two during the high-speed chase in the Reckless Pursuit chapter. The Dread Axe is amazing here, as you can charge it and tank hits before unleashing a combo that’ll crush the Shadow Warden.

Ring the Valley Sha-Chi Tower 1st Floor bell after winning the fight. It reveals two more bow loot spots on the map, as well as a closed door that you can’t open just yet.

Three Maskwalkers attack as soon as you enter the Steel Tower. They emerge from the fire surrounding the central furnace. These bronze men have skin that acts as a shield, so you need to use the Dread Axe to destroy their armor before attacking.

There are three collectibles to pick up on this first floor: Primal Stone Records: Sha-Chi Tower Investigation Report , To My Husband, Huang Miao , and Perfect Transcension . Stand in front of the stairs on the right side of the room to see the first two collectibles, then walk to the back side of the room to see the third.

You’ll notice some candles near a secret path in the second image above. It leads to an area underneath the tower where you’ll find an optional boss and the Flesh Lily Fields bell . The boss fight rewards you with the Scarlet Wraithblade – a two-handed weapon that can slow enemies and deal damage with spider lilies. This is also where you find Twin Flesh Lilies for Yu’er’s Flesh Lily side quest.

You can find collectibles titled The Matchmaker’s Advice and A Reply From Hua’s Father along this low path. You’ll find others titled Letter From Hua , To My Husband, Liu Shangli , To My Dear Husband, Jia Qianqiu , and A Reckless Invitation around the boss battlefield as well.

This walkthrough will continue along the main path, up the Steel Tower, but you should prepare yourself for a difficult fight against Hua, Deadly Betrothed if you decide to take that detour here. Flesh Lily Fields Bell

Hua, Deadly Betrothed, is a tough optional boss, but the detour to the Flesh Lily Fields is well worth it for the bell, Yu’er’s quest item, a strong new weapon, and six collectibles.

When ready, return to the first floor of the Steel Tower and head up the stairs next to the furnace to face a new enemy type: the Maskwalker Powderkeg . Powderkegs are slow-moving enemies that deal serious damage by exploding after they die, so the Feather Bow is a safe final hit from a distance.

The corridor splits after you beat the Powderkeg. One path goes upward while the other goes out onto the roof. Collect the Remnant Dust on the roof, then climb up the scratched ledge to reach the next floor.

There are a few items to pick up on this floor. There are x2 Twinned Metal behind the ramp you used to reach the floor, x444 Remnant Dust in front of the ramp, and the Transcension collectible around the corner.

Three bronze Maskwalkers appear when you get near the steel pillar in the center of the room. Defeat them, then climb the stairs next to the pillar to face another Powderkeg. Bait it, then back up if the explosive on its back starts flashing. That means it’s about to explode.

A collectible titled What Is Sha-Chi? is hiding behind the Powderkeg, and you can also pick up x220 Remnant Dust near the next set of stairs.

Walk up to the next floor to find the Valley Sha-Chi Tower Summit bell . Ring it, then speak to the Watchful Shadow Warden to the right.

Shadow Wardens are usually forced to obey the Order, but he says that he broke free of the Mindseal by ingesting a Primal Stone – a source of energy used to power Transcension like these. This conversation adds the A Severed Mindseal side quest to your log.

Climb the scratched walls next to the Shadow Warden to ascend a bit more, then approach the glowing orange item on the other side of the roof.

The glowing orange item is the lost key from the purple Deep in the Valley quest. You can’t reach it just yet, but there’s x886 Remnant Dust below it.

Follow the path along the wooden bridge and down a ladder to find a lone Shadow Warden. Defeat him to obtain the Sha-Chi Furnace Inspection Crank.

Pick up the x2 Forged Metal inside the large pipe next to the ladder you just used, then climb down the ladder near where you fought the Shadow Warden.

Turn to the right as soon as you descend the ladder. You’ll find another ladder that you can kick down to create a shortcut leading back to the first floor where you initially entered the tower. You can use this shortcut to reattach the Sha-Chi Furnace Inspection Crank to the furnace on the tower’s first floor, but we’re continuing on toward the Hunt.

Turn back in the other direction to pick up a collectible titled Comments on the Pillars of Kunlun next to a campfire. You can also speak to the collapsing Mandate Disciple there to add the Pillars of Kunlun purple quest to your log.

From there, follow the left path to reach the Waterfall Bridge bell . Defeat the group of Maskwalkers down the stairs in front of the bell, but watch out for the arsonist, shielded brute, and twin-axe brute.

Before crossing the bridge, you can look left to find x3 Broadplate Metal in a cage. There’s also a ladder to the right that leads down to a small area where you’ll find a Weapon Reforge Talisman, x3 Forged Metal, x3 Broadplate Metal, and x770 Remnant Dust.

Cross the wooden waterfall bridge when ready, and walk through the cave, picking up x775 Remnant Dust along the way. The Great Warterfall bell is right in front of the boss arena where the Hunt is waiting.

Boss Battle: The Hunt, Hunter of the Order

It’s time to settle the score against the Hunt in front of the Great Waterfall. This time, you’re fighting on solid ground instead of a moving cart. Some of his moves should feel familiar, but here are the special attacks you need to look out for:

The Hunt can attack from most ranges with wild chain sickle moves. Parrying will lower his Sha-Chi meter quickly, but if you’re not confident in the timings, just block until you see a blue or red flash attack. And switch weapons defensively to refill your Sha-Chi meter if it runs low while blocking.

Offensively, you can overwhelm the Hunt, especially if you obtained the Scarlet Wraithblade from the optional boss battle against Hua, Deadly Betrothed. It creates patches of Red Spider Lilies that drain the Hunt’s health if he stands in them during both Sha-Chi combos and Power Surges. And sometimes, a button prompt pops up during longer combos, giving you chances to deal extra damage.

The Hunt regains all of his HP once you fully deplete his health bar. This is phase two, against The Hunt, Sixfold Scythe . He now has extra arms that come with new attacks, so here are all of the new special moves that you should watch out for.

The Hunt has more arms in this phase, which means he has more sickles to launch your way. The attacks are a bit quicker and can hit you from a greater distance. He also has a slow-moving projectile that hits multiple times.

Your strategy doesn’t need to change much offensively – you can still overwhelm the boss. Just try not to overextend your combos, especially when you see the Hunt’s Sha-Chi meter refill.

You’re rewarded with the Hunter’s Chain Sickle Phantom Edge after the fight. It can perform long-range combos in battle, and it allows you to grapple onto high points outside of battle.

You can now access several new high points across the map to complete side quests and find rare items. The Hunter’s Chain Sickle can be used to grab the lost key for the Deep in the Valley purple quest, opening up the large area in the center of the map.

When ready, head through the cave behind the Great Waterfall. Take the first right when you see a fire to find an Exotic Copper Ingot and a collectible titled Reply to a Request for Aid at a dead end.

Return to the fire and climb up the scratched wall. Follow the linear path and pick up a collectible titled The Discordance at the toppled shrine before using the Hunter’s Chain Sickle to reach the high ledge.

Now, follow the fires, picking up x3 Solvent and x2 Phantom Edge Reforge Talismans and a Traversal Talisman along the way.

The Steel and Steam chapter ends as you approach the cave exit. A scene also plays, showing a cart passing a drunk man on the road one day earlier. Next up, we have the Snake’s Reflection chapter.

articles.title: Things Phantom Blade Zero Doesn’t Tell You - Phantom Blade Zero Guide - IGN
articles.summary: One thing Phantom Blade Zero makes very clear is that pretty much everything wants to kill you. Sure, you’ve got a sword and some slick moves to help
articles.body:
One thing Phantom Blade Zero makes very clear is that pretty much everything wants to kill you. Sure, you’ve got a sword and some slick moves to help you fight back, but it doesn’t tell you a whole lot outside of that. Fortunately, you’ve got a deeper bag of tricks than you might realize. Here are nine things Phantom Blade Zero doesn’t tell you, with plenty of tips to help you fight back.

9 Things Phantom Blade Zero Doesn’t Tell You

You'll burn through a lot of Sha-chi while attacking and defending, making it easier to break your guard and vulnerable to a quick trip to an early grave. You could let it regenerate naturally, but enemies often won’t give you that time given the quick pace of combat. Instead, when you find your Sha-chi meter nearly depleted, switch your weapons.

While the game does tell you, briefly, that switching weapons instantly refills your supply of Sha-chi, it does not emphasize how absolutely critical this particular mechanic is to your success. Use this method to fuel your attacks, or to replenish your defense when the enemy is on the verge of breaking your guard. Eventually you can unlock a faster cooldown on weapon switching, enabling you to quickly chain back and forth between your weapons, and keep your Sha-chi topped off as you do. If an enemy is about to recover from a guard break, you may be better off switching weapons and stopping your attack early so you can be ready to defend.

You can tell if the enemy is close to a guard break by the yellow meter by it, or in a boss's case, beneath its name. Keep an eye on its regeneration to know when to switch back on the defensive.

The flashy and brutal finishers are one of the best elements of Phantom Blade Zero’s combat, and they have one major benefit beyond just removing enemies in satisfyingly gruesome ways.

To perform a finisher, look for a button prompt to pop up while attacking an enemy.

Soul is completely invulnerable to incoming attacks during finishers. So, while it may be tempting to pull off a stylish kill the second you see the prompt, a bit of patience is often rewarded. If you can hold off for a few extra seconds to time it during incoming attacks, setting you up to avoid damage completely.

A lot of your core adventure will revolve around slaughtering legions of baddies as you go from point A to point B, but when it comes to exploration, Phantom Blade Zero is much more like a metroidvania. Pathways in every region will be blocked by barriers that keep them shut until you find just the right tool, which means you won’t be one-hundred percenting areas before moving on. But you should come back when you can, as these barriers often hide upgrade materials, quest items, and even secret bosses, often with brand new weapons for you when you beat them. So take advantage of backtracking once you get the items to unblock these paths.

You have a lot of freedom to work on the main story or work on cleaning up sidequests, but that comes with a warning: some sidequests eventually disappear if you don’t do them on time. One example is gathering medicines for Yu’er. She’ll move on to new areas depending on where you are in the main quest, and when she does, there’s no going back once she does. If you are a completionist, you’ll want to make sure you’ve progressed each side quest as far as you can before finishing the main mission in each area, or you could miss out on valuable goodies.

Soul Remnants, metals, and other upgrade materials can feel stingy at times, but that doesn’t mean your chance to experiment with new weapons is necessarily limited.

Every weapon , Phantom Edge , and Accessory lets you upgrade it to level 10, then revert it back down, returning everything that was spent and consumed in the process. Don’t ignore this, stripping one weapon to try out a new toy is the best way to find which weapons work for you. After level ten, and again after level twenty, you’ll need to use a special consumable to revert, but these are plentiful enough that you should feel comfortable using them as needed. Keep in mind that Phantom Edges and standard weapons require different consumables to respec once you hit those upgrade thresholds.

Upgrading new weapons and experimenting is extremely important, for while combat can seem simple at first, with only two buttons for attacking (one for standard, and one for Sha-chi) much of the depth of each weapon comes with their alternate abilities or properties that are often unlocked by reaching certain upgrade thresholds. For instance, when you get Jagged Steel to level 5, you unlock a special attack that can inflict massive Bleed buildup to enemies who are guard broken.

At level 5, Sanguine and Sanguine Twin allow you to buff your weapons for 20 seconds to greatly increase damage. These upgradeable perks even extend to Phantom Edges. Dread Axe at level 5 unlocks the ability to immediately perform a fully charged strike by double tapping R2 or the Right Trigger and spending two Remnant Sparks. And Hunter’s Chain Sickle gives a Scorpion-like yank that pulls enemies in after a combo.

An important thing to note is that while you can see what you need to upgrade a weapon to unlock certain abilities on the upgrade equipment screen, if you’re looking at them in your inventory, you need to press the highlighted "Advanced" button to go into the advanced tab.

Many Upgrades come later than you might expect

You have a lot of things to upgrade in your journey. From your weapons, to your accessories, medicines, phantom edges , and Soul himself. However, what you can upgrade and when depends on pick ups and vendors scattered throughout the entire game. Be prepared to gather upgrade materials, like the ones for medicines or accessories, and not be able to use them until later. General rule of thumb, if you don’t know how to upgrade something, just keep playing and eventually the game will tell you. We also have another video on how to upgrade weapons, accessories, and medicines.

As you explore the world of the Wulin, you’ll come across scrolls, shrines, and other intractable objects. These are great for fleshing out the world, learning about characters, and understanding the various factions warring throughout the land. But it often comes with another important benefit too: Remnant Dust, your do-it-all upgrade currency. Anytime you see the glowing light indicating a scroll, or you see the button prompt for Soul to investigate a person or object, there’s a good chance you’ll earn free XP to upgrade your character and weapons, and you might even learn a thing or two along the way.

I know “Soulslike” is a very loaded term and comes with a lot of baggage, and Phantom Blade Zero may bear a few of the markers of the Soulslike genre, but it is very much its own thing. For one, enemies don’t respawn after touching bells, Phantom Blade’s equivalent of Bonfires. And while bosses can be tough, and definitely act as difficulty spikes and skill checks throughout the adventure, some will even skip the first phase on retries if you die after getting to later phases. All in all, Phantom Blade Zero is an action game with a few Soulslike trappings. And really, who cares at the end of the day. Are you having fun? That’s all that matters.

Armed with this knowledge, and few trusty weapons, you should be well prepared to take on all manner of murderous baddies. Just make sure to upgrade your weapons, medicines, and trinkets while you are at it.

articles.title: Emotional Brewers pitcher Jacob Misiorowski reacts to Milwaukee’s historic World Series win
articles.summary: Jacob Misiorowski delivered the biggest start in Milwaukee Brewers history, and when it was over, he could barely put the moment into words. Misiorowski toss...
articles.body:
Jacob Misiorowski delivered the biggest start in Milwaukee Brewers history, and when it was over, he could barely put the moment into words. Misiorowski tossed 5 2/3 scoreless innings as the Brewers beat the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 in Game 5 on Wednesday night at Tropicana Field, clinching the first World Series title in franchise history.

Speaking to FOX Sports after the final out, the young right-hander was overcome with emotion.

"I don't even have words. You know, it's amazing. You know, just watching my guys celebrate," Misiorowski said. "You know, in this city. I know they're going crazy in Milwaukee. It's awesome."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

When asked about his message to the fans in Milwaukee and Wisconsin, Misiorowski fought back tears. "They've been nothing but support for us this whole year and years prior, and it's been amazing," Misiorowski said. "I'm getting emotional."

The 24-year-old knew coming into the night that he had a chance to pitch the clincher, and he credited his catcher for helping him handle the moment.

"I couldn't have done it without him. And it's been amazing with him this whole season," Misiorowski said.

The flamethrower lived up to the billing. He allowed just two hits and reached 100 mph on 51 of his 86 pitches, including two pitches that hit 103 mph in the first inning. He exited with a four-run lead in the sixth after dealing with a cramp in his right calf . Trevor Megill handled the final two innings, getting Richie Palacios to ground out to end it.

The title came one night after the Rays avoided a sweep with a 12-inning walk-off win in Game 4. Misiorowski made sure there would be no further drama.

It caps a remarkable season for the 24-year-old , who went 16-5 with a 1.80 ERA and 252 strikeouts in the regular season. He led the majors in ERA, strikeouts and opponents' batting average, and he is widely expected to win the NL Cy Young Award next month .

The championship is the first for Milwaukee since the Braves won it all in 1957. The Brewers finished the regular season with a franchise-record 103 wins and went 11-2 in the postseason, knocking off the San Diego Padres, Los Angeles Dodgers and Rays.

For Misiorowski and the Brewers, the wait is finally over.

articles.title: Rays manager Kevin Cash gives Brewers’ bullpen its flowers after crushing World Series loss
articles.summary: The Tampa Bay Rays came up short in the World Series, but Kevin Cash was not shy about giving credit where it was due. After the Milwaukee Brewers closed out...
articles.body:
The Tampa Bay Rays came up short in the World Series, but Kevin Cash was not shy about giving credit where it was due. After the Milwaukee Brewers closed out a 4-1 win in Game 5 on Wednesday night at Tropicana Field to capture the first championship in franchise history, the Rays manager singled out the unit that gave his team fits all series long.

Cash said the Brewers have "as elite of a bullpen as I've ever seen," via MLB Network .

It is hard to argue with him. Milwaukee's relievers were a constant thorn in Tampa Bay's side , repeatedly slamming the door in close games and stranding runners in big spots.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Aaron Ashby was the headliner. The left-hander did not allow a run through his first 15 2/3 innings of the postseason, putting him second all-time for the most consecutive scoreless innings to begin a postseaso n, behind only Andrew Miller's 16 in 2016. He also collected three saves, including the final out of Game 2 with the tying run on third base .

Trevor Megill and Abner Uribe were just as reliable at the back end. Megill survived a tense ninth inning in Game 1, striking out Jonny DeLuca after a game-ending double play was overturned on replay. Uribe, meanwhile, picked up the win in Game 2 with 1 1/3 hitless innings.

The bullpen came through once again in the clincher. Jacob Misiorowski tossed 5 2/3 scoreless innings before exiting with a cramp in his right calf, and Milwaukee's relievers took it from there. Tampa Bay finally scratched across a run in the ninth, but Megill closed it out when Richie Palacios grounded out to end the series.

Cash's comments carry extra weight coming from a manager who has built his reputation on bullpen management . The Rays have long been known for their deep, creative relief corps, and Bryan Baker anchored their own bullpen with 41 saves this season.

Still, there was no answering Milwaukee. The Brewers won three games in the series by three runs or fewer, with their bullpen protecting late leads each time.

The Rays will head into the offseason looking to bounce back, while the Brewers can celebrate a championship that their relief corps helped deliver.
